solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Set off full of beans, ready to start a fight

parts.note: to set off a gun or alarm is to trigger it
someone full of beans is lively and cheerful, i.e. happy

explanation.surface: Someone sets off in high spirits, spoiling for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick to shoot or quarrel is described by this idiom, so it fits a person itching for a fight.

clue.text: Hung around, bound to cover arrival

indicators.note: to cover means the word for bound goes around the other piece

parts.note: bound means tied up
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrival

explanation.surface: Someone tied up waiting for a delivery to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hung around is to have lingered, a synonym of this verb.

clue.text: What the journalist said to have an impact

definitions.meaning: a reporter introducing themselves might say ...
to make a strong impression on someone

explanation.definitionFit: To make a strong mark on someone is to make them admire you, and it also splits as I'm press.

clue.text: Redhead takes the biscuit!

definitions.meaning: ginger means red-haired and nut is slang for the head
a crisp spiced biscuit flavoured with ginger

explanation.surface: A red-haired person behaves outrageously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being outrageous; here it just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a ginger-flavoured British biscuit, and literally a red head.

clue.text: Man made?

parts.note: read as a manufactured man, an artificial humanoid machine

explanation.definitionFit: A machine built in human form is literally a man that has been made.

clue.text: A job the French gave early Christian

parts.note: a post is a position or job
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French employer gives a job to an early Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of Christ's twelve disciples sent out to preach was an early Christian.

clue.text: Plant found in favourite area around university

indicators.note: around means the first pieces go around the next

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A plant grows in a favourite spot near the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: This brightly flowered garden annual is a plant.

clue.text: What might cushion amazement — a robber's plan

parts.note: shock is sudden amazement

indicators.note: plan, as a verb, means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A robber plots to soften the surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' rearranges A ROBBERS into the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's damper exists to cushion jolts.

clue.text: Puts questions to angry divorcee in same fashion

parts.note: cross means angry
a former spouse is an ex

indicators.note: fashion, as a verb, means the letters of in same are reshaped

explanation.surface: An angry divorcee interrogates their former partner the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, a lawyer interrogating the other side's witness puts questions to them.

clue.text: Layer of subsoil difficult to sift

parts.note: something difficult is hard
to pan is to sift gravel for gold in a shallow dish

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that a compacted soil layer is a nightmare to sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: This term names a compacted, impervious layer lying below the topsoil.

clue.text: Herring or puffer fish?

definitions.meaning: a herring cured by smoking whole
playfully, something that puffs up or swells, as a fish might

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a smoked herring and, read literally, anything that bloats up like a puffer.

clue.text: Oriental revolutionary's crossed lines without leader

indicators.note: Che has the lines crossing through him, so his name is cut open to hold them

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary; the 's means has

indicators.note: the word lines loses its first letter, its leader

explanation.surface: An Eastern revolutionary's lines have been crossed out, missing their first one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed' looks like a verb about cancelling lines, but here it means the revolutionary's name is crossed by, so wrapped around, the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental here is an adjective for something from the Far East, as Chinese is.

clue.text: Outwardly tense time before a star returns from sickness

indicators.note: outwardly asks for only the outside letters of the word tense
returns tells us the word for a star is read backwards

parts.note: the sun is our star

explanation.surface: A tense moment before a celebrity comes back after being unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' looks like it describes the tension; it only asks for the outer letters of 'tense'. 'returns' applies only to the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is a bacterial disease, so this infection counts as a sickness.

clue.text: Turning back, eased naturally outside range

indicators.note: Turning back says the hidden letters are read backwards
outside says the answer's letters lie on the outer edges of the two words, end of one and start of the next

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone eases off as they head back out of range.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'outside range' as the definition, but the Andes are the range itself; 'outside' marks the letters straddling the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The great mountain chain of South America is a range.

clue.text: French landmark one dreamt about

indicators.note: about signals the letters of one dreamt are moved around

explanation.surface: A tourist says they once dreamt of a famous sight in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris cathedral on the Île de la Cité is one of France's best-known sights.

clue.text: Put an end to insect found across North Australia

indicators.note: across means the insect's name stretches over the other piece

parts.note: a termite is an insect
N is north and A is Australia

explanation.surface: An insect found across northern Australia must be exterminated.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to finish it or put an end to it.

clue.text: Evidence of humour by Spain's first butcher

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of Spain's

parts.note: laughter shows that something has been found funny

explanation.surface: A Spanish butcher's shop rings with merriment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the first letter of Spain next to the laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to massacre them, a verb sense shared with this word.

clue.text: Noise suppressed by a boy's magic rubber

indicators.note: in a down clue, being suppressed by places this piece below the others

parts.note: a lad is a boy
din is loud noise

explanation.surface: A boy's eraser is quietened by a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: The rubber is the man who rubbed the magic lamp in the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk tale he rubs a lamp to summon a genie, so he is a magic rubber.

clue.text: Biker could be comparatively oily without one

indicators.note: without means the piece for one is taken out

parts.note: more oily is greasier
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist might be oilier, though not by one.
explanation.definitionFit: A greaser is slang for a leather-clad motorcyclist with slicked hair.

clue.text: A little backward eating one's bone

indicators.note: eating means the reversed pair swallows the next piece
backward says the pair a and little are read in reverse order

parts.note: a little is a bit
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A slightly slow person chewing on their own bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns A BIT into TIBA; 'eating' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone of the lower leg is this bone.

clue.text: Almost making a mistake in case of the meat dish

indicators.note: in means the shortened piece goes inside the outer letters
case of asks for the outside letters of the
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: erring means making a mistake

explanation.surface: A cook nearly gets the meat dish wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of the' looks like part of the meat dish's description, but it asks for the two letters casing 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coarse pâté cooked in an earthenware dish, a meat dish.

clue.text: Council regulations covering some aspects of cricket?

definitions.meaning: local rules made by a council
the laws covering byes, runs scored when the ball passes the batter and keeper

explanation.definitionFit: These are local regulations, and punningly the laws governing byes in cricket.

clue.text: Lecturers study royal protocols at last

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of protocols

explanation.surface: Academics pore over court etiquette, finally.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities, a reader is a senior lecturer below professor.

clue.text: Lord North's warning?

parts.note: sire is a form of address to a lord or king

explanation.surface: A northern nobleman gives a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a loud warning signal.

clue.text: Former Prime Minister executed by one from the Middle East

indicators.note: executed means beheaded here, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: A former premier is put to death by a man from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Israel is a person from the Middle East.

clue.text: Rudeness mostly transforms consumer

indicators.note: transforms says the remaining letters change into a new order
mostly means the last letter of rudeness is dropped

explanation.surface: Being rude changes a customer for the worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts RUDENESS to RUDENES, which 'transforms' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The final person who uses a product is its consumer.

clue.text: Stir up trouble at gate 1

indicators.note: trouble, read as a verb, means the letters are disturbed

parts.note: 1 is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: There is a disturbance at the first gate at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The I from '1' joins AT GATE before 'trouble' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up feelings or a liquid is to agitate it.

clue.text: Charges levied by hypnotists

parts.note: admission charges, reread as the money a hypnotist earns for putting people in a trance

explanation.definitionFit: These are admission charges, and a hypnotist's trance-inducing work punningly earns the same name.
